name: Resistor Environment QA 4
description: Multiple choice question about electricity, resistors and current QA: Flow of current through ammeter in parallel resistor circuit

examples.input: Five identical lamps, each with resistance of \SI{1100}{\ohm}, are connected in a ladder network configuration to a \SI{1100}{\ohm}  supply. The circuit is structured with a main supply line (the rail) running horizontally from the \SI{1100}{\ohm}  source, with five resistors serving as rungs that branch off from this main rail at successive junction points along its length. Each rung connects from a junction point on the main rail to a common return line (ground/neutral). Current flows from the \SI{220}{\volt} supply along the main rail, and as it travels, it encounters five junction points where each lamp branches off sequentially. An ammeter is positioned in the main rail itself, specifically after the first two rungs have branched off but before the last three rungs split off. This means the ammeter measures the current in the main rail that continues forward to supply the last three lamps, after the first two lamps have already drawn their current from the supply. What current does the ammeter read?
